requirements.requirement: Remote ingress rejects unauthenticated MCP requests.
Device bridge rejects unauthenticated device registration.
A connected device is selected explicitly or by configured default.
At most four workstation-effect requests execute concurrently per device.
Execution-lane concurrency is demonstrated against a real WorkBridge-qualified DesktopCommander payload, not inferred from a queue unit test.
Up to 32 independently identified logic work contexts may be active; logic identity is distinct from effect authority.
A logic lane must bind an explicit device before workstation effect dispatch.
Concurrent client JSON-RPC IDs cannot collide inside the workstation bridge.
Packaged Node and DesktopCommander entrypoint hashes are checked before process launch.
The WorkBridge manifest is authenticated against trusted provenance rather than trusted solely because it is local.
Disconnect rejects in-flight requests and reconnect does not silently replay them.
Real MCP initialize/tools-list/call round trip succeeds through remote ingress and device bridge.
Windows device-agent operation is exercised on CI or equivalent clean Windows runner.
requirements.note: Windows CI builds/tests the TypeScript implementation and parses the PowerShell launcher; full live workstation execution remains integration evidence.

requirements.requirement: Production endpoint, OAuth/device pairing, deployment, and activation remain separate effect claims.
